title: Compare two out-of-office replies
context: You're on leave for a week, and customers email you about their orders.

a: I am currently out of the office with limited access to email until Monday, October 14.
If your matter is urgent, please contact the office.
I apologize for any inconvenience and will respond as soon as possible on my return.
b: I'm away until Monday, October 14, and not reading email.
For an urgent order, call Jo Mensah at 514-⁠555-⁠0142.
For anything else, I'll reply when I'm back.

qualities.question: Which sentence tells a customer with an urgent order exactly who to call?
qualities.reason: Jo's name and number let a customer with an urgent order act today, not in a week. "Contact the office" gives no name and no number.
qualities.note: Who to call for an urgent order

qualities.question: Which sentence says what counts as an urgent order?
qualities.reason: Both replies mention urgency, and neither says what counts, so each customer has to guess whether to call.

qualities.question: Which sentence says plainly whether you'll read email while you're away?
qualities.reason: "Not reading email" tells customers not to wait for an answer. Version A's "limited access" leaves them hoping for one.
